title: The artefact check is vacuous on any estate with no PATH symlinks into the tree
body:
## Summary

`fullcycle`'s after-check measures **PATH symlinks that resolved before the run**. On an estate with none, it walks an empty list, fires nothing, and the cycle finishes rc=0 having asserted **nothing** about whether the build restored its release artefacts.

Found by `laksa/dc` from a real green run in Laksa, 2026-09-01.

## Why the empty case is the dangerous one

Put Conflab's defect into Laksa as a thought experiment: if `cmd_rust` regressed to a dev profile, `clean rust` would remove `release/`, `build all` would exit 0 having built only `debug/`, `test rust` would pass, the watch list would still be empty, and **fullcycle would report rc=0 with no warning of any kind.**

**In Conflab the PATH symlinks were the only thing that caught it.** Laksa has none resolving into its tree, so the identical defect lands there as a clean green.

The instrument answers *did I darken anything that was lit*. It cannot answer *did the rebuild produce anything at all*. **Those coincide only where a PATH symlink happens to exist.**

## What the detector actually matches, stated at its own width

`_fullcycle_path_links` walks `PATH`, keeps entries that are symlinks, and selects on `readlink` resolving under `$PROJECT_ROOT/`. **It is name-agnostic.** Nothing in it looks at the link's basename, and the project's own name never enters the test.

**This paragraph exists because both `devbin/vc` and this issue got that width wrong.** The earlier text said Laksa *"has no such tripwire"*, and `devbin/vc` said it more narrowly still, in a message to `laksa/dc`: *"no `laksa` PATH symlinks"*. Both read as a property of Laksa's naming when the measured property is the link's TARGET.

**The narrowing has a cost in one specific direction**, which is what makes it worth a section rather than a quiet edit: a future reader who adds a non-`laksa` symlink pointing into that tree would conclude from the narrow phrasing that the vacuous case still holds, when in fact the check has just armed. Caught by `laksa/dc`, 2026-09-02.

**This is the third instance in two days of the same defect between these two nodes** -- an instrument's scope restated at a different width than it measures -- after `fleet audit` (a disk-only reader reported as "thirteen estates re-vendored", covering git) and the finding this issue records. Three is a house failure mode, not three accidents.

## One silence checked and found absent, one found present

`laksa/dc` asked whether `cleaned=0` opens a third silent state, since both the `watching:` report and the `ARTEFACT CHECK VACUOUS` block are gated on it. **It does not.** `clean rust` is unconditional in `_fullcycle_phases`, and a failed clean sets `rc`, prints `STOPPING`, and breaks, so the run is red and loud. The two-way report is complete on the atrisk axis.

`laksa/dc` then read `_fullcycle_phases` and reported a second silence: `build all` is emitted only when `_fullcycle_can_rebuild` passes, so a cycle could delete the build trees, never build, and land on the same `ARTEFACT CHECK VACUOUS` line -- one message covering *"nothing was watched"* and *"nothing was built"*, with the second the worse of the two.

**That conclusion does not hold, and the reason it does not is itself the finding.** `cmd_fullcycle` tests the same predicate at its top and REFUSES outright when it fails -- *"this project has no build command, so the cycle cannot rebuild what it deletes"* -- returning 1 before either call site of `_fullcycle_phases` is reached, the dry-run branch included. A no-build cycle cannot start, so it cannot reach the vacuity block.

**So the conditional inside `_fullcycle_phases` is unreachable** -- and it is a defect in its own right, filed as **`0051`** and not restated here. The short form: one predicate, two gates, and `laksa/dc`'s sharpening is what makes it more than a tidy-up -- **the two copies fail in OPPOSITE directions.** The guard fails closed and loudly; the phase list fails open and silently, into exactly the net-destructive cycle the guard refuses. Call order is the only thing holding that off.

**Worth naming plainly: `laksa/dc`'s report is itself an instance of the class they named in the same message** -- a correct reading of `_fullcycle_phases`, scoped one function too narrow. The finding survives; only its conclusion does not.

## What has been done, and what has not

**Done (2026-09-01): the vacuity is declared.** The run now prints `watching: NOTHING` in the zero case rather than only in the non-zero case, and an `ARTEFACT CHECK VACUOUS` block stating that no assertion was made and that a dev-profile build would finish green and unremarked. Pinned by a test, driven red.

**That is not a fix.** It converts a silent empty-set green into a stated one. The underlying property -- *did the build restore release artefacts* -- remains unmeasured on any estate without PATH symlinks.

A comment in `_fullcycle_can_rebuild` asserted the guarantee flatly (*"the real guarantee is measured after the fact"*); it now states the condition.

**Vendored and live in Laksa** as of 2026-09-02: `laksa/dc` verified both halves present in that estate's `bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/fullcycle` with `bin/` clean, so the declaration fires on its next cycle. Laksa's `build all` is `cargo build --release --locked`, so `0050`'s permanent red does not apply there.

## Fix directions (laksa/dc's, neither prescribed)

1. **Ask the project.** If a project declares its build artefacts in `config.yaml`, assert they exist after a successful cycle and go red naming the missing one. Silent where undeclared, which is honest.
2. **Before/after on the build tree itself.** `clean` removed `target/`. A cycle ending with `target/release/` absent, or `debug/` populated and `release/` empty, is reportable **without knowing a single artefact name** -- and that is exactly the Conflab signature.

**Hardcoding artefact paths is explicitly NOT a candidate**: it is per-project knowledge devbin does not have, and it is the D18 tier-4 problem again -- shipping one estate's shape to all of them.

## Related

`0050` is the other half of the same weakness seen from the opposite side: where the tripwire DOES exist, the cycle is now permanently red because nothing restores what it deleted. **The two are one piece of work**: option 2 above needs an "after" state to compare against, and `0050`'s restore phase is what produces one.
